recentItems.title: How to overcome your unhappiness reflex #shorts #tedx
Why love alone can't save your relationship | Stan Tatkin | TEDxKC
recentItems.description:
Psychotherapist and Couple Expert Stan Tatkin argues that when couples fight, the real issue is almost never what they're fighting about — it's what happens in their nervous systems when either partner is under stress. Drawing on decades of clinical work, he shows how our brains mistake prediction for danger, turning the people we love into perceived threats. His answer isn't more love, but a consciously designed relationship: shared purpose, agreed-upon principles, and a plan for repair before the next conflict even arrives.

 tan Tatkin, PsyD, MFT, is a clinician, researcher, teacher, and developer of A Psychobiological Approach to Couple Therapy® (PACT). He has a clinical practice in Calabasas, CA. With his wife, Dr. Tracey Tatkin, he co-founded the PACT Institute for the purpose of training other mental health professionals worldwide, along with a growing PACT faculty, to use this method in their clinical practice. Together, Stan and Tracey also lead couple workshops.

Stan is a recently retired teacher and supervisor of family medicine residents at Kaiser Permanente, Woodland Hills, CA, and is an associate clinical professor at the UCLA David Geffen School of Medicine, Department of Family Medicine for more than 20 years. He is on the board of directors of Lifespan Learning Institute and served as a member on Relationships First Counsel, a nonprofit organization founded by Harville Hendrix and Helen LaKelly Hunt. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: You don’t have a savings problem. You have a system problem. | Steve Short & Mark Schlipman | TEDxKC
recentItems.description:
Most of us eventually learn how to save money — but almost none of us learn how to teach it. In this talk, Mark Schlipman and Steve Short reveal why 85% of Americans over 45 wish they'd started saving sooner, and argue the real problem isn't knowledge, it's habit. Using a simple budgeting framework and the same logic you'd use to teach a kid to brush their teeth, they lay out a system parents, mentors, and employers can use to help the next generation build financial literacy and savings habits early — before they ever have the chance to fall behind.

 Steve Short is a retired C-suite executive, strategic advisor, and co-author of the best-selling personal finance book The Simple Road Toward Financial Freedom. He spent nearly 30 years at Enterprise Holdings, where he rose from Management Trainee to Vice President, ultimately leading a $3B+ division and helping drive more than $2B in growth through innovation, partnerships, and customer-focused strategy.

He later served as Chief Marketing Officer at Cordell & Cordell / Lexicon, where he led marketing and sales efforts across multiple brands and helped drive revenue growth and operational improvements during a period of significant change.

Today, Steve advises organizations on strategy, growth, and innovation, including emerging applications of AI in the travel industry. He is also focused on financial literacy, using his platform to help young adults and professionals develop simple, structured approaches to managing money.

Steve Short is a retired C-suite executive, strategic advisor. recentItems.title: Identity comes before output | Ken Cardwell | TEDxBeverly Grove
recentItems.description:
Digital systems architect Ken Cardwell opened his TEDxBeverlyGrove 2026 talk by asking the audience to imagine a deepfake video of themselves, saying and doing things they never said or did, created entirely from photos and clips they had already posted online. What followed was not a warning about technology. It was an argument about identity itself. Drawing on his patents in synthetic identity binding and his work building governed systems for digital presence, Cardwell closes with the line that gives the talk its title: identity comes before output. Ken Cardwell is a founder and systems architect working at the intersection of identity, artificial intelligence, and human representation. He is the founder of ActorForge and the Virtual Actors Guild, where he is building early infrastructures for governed synthetic performers—digital entities designed to operate with defined identity, consent, authorship, and lifecycle control. Ken has filed multiple provisional patents spanning synthetic identity binding, delegated presence, lifecycle management, and platform authorization frameworks, focused on making digital representation accountable in an age of programmable identity. 

At TEDxBeverlyGrove
Ken Cardwell will share The Identity First Rule—a decision test for what must be true before we hand voice, judgment, and representation to digital systems. The risk isn’t “bad content.” It’s the moment assistance becomes impersonation. He’ll outline the guardrails that keep authorship, consent, and accountability attached to a real person. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Living with Purpose - Distilled into eleven words | Joyce Ng | TEDxBrownU
recentItems.description: How do you move on after a tragedy? In this talk, Joyce Ng shares three simple ways to transform personal hardship into a life of purpose. As a survivor of the 9/11 attacks and also a student at Brown University during the mass shooting, Joyce discusses her experiences on how to live with purpose that can be distilled into eleven words. Joyce works in a leadership role at Google, driven by a mission to build things that matter, while pursuing a Master’s degree at Brown. Beyond her career, her most profound impact lies in her advocacy. As the founder of a nonprofit supporting the 9/11 community and author of the history book Hotel 9/11, she has transformed her experience of survival into a lasting legacy of support and historical preservation. recentItems.title: How can we bridge the mental health gap? | Devashis Jena | TEDxKLH Bachupally
recentItems.description:
Our relationship with money is shaped by more than just income, it is influenced by psychology, social media, marketing, and everyday spending habits. This talk explores the hidden forces behind our purchasing decisions, from ₹99 pricing and irresistible offers to instant gratification and social influence. It challenges us to distinguish between needs and wants, build financial discipline, and make more conscious decisions about saving and investing. Ultimately, it asks a simple question: Are we spending our money, or are we being persuaded to spend it? "Devashis Jena is an entrepreneur, changemaker, and public speaker working at the intersection of mental health, social impact, entrepreneurship, and storytelling.

He is the Founder & CEO of Project C Foundation, an international mental health organisation that he built from Hyderabad and has expanded across eight countries. Through Project C, he has worked to build accessible mental health initiatives and partnerships, creating a broader ecosystem around emotional well-being and support.

Devashis is also the Founder of In Conversation With Dev (ICWD), a storytelling platform that brings together founders, business leaders, athletes, creators, artists, and changemakers to explore the people and stories behind their achievements.

As an entrepreneur, Devashis has worked across strategic partnerships, community building, business growth, brand strategy, and organisational development, building collaborations and communities that connect people, ideas, and opportunities. recentItems.title: Value Beyond the Gold Coast. | Abanga Azumah Prosper | TEDxUniversityofCapeCoast
recentItems.description:
In this very insightful piece, Abanga highlights the experience of the average northern student studying in the south. He goes on to expound on how since colonial times the nation had percieved value only by the natural resources it possessed which was located more in the south than in the northern province, thereby creating an unappreciation and devaluation of the northern provinces and its people. However he brought a new perception and way of looking at the north that revealed that it had the most valuable asset of all which is the human resource. Abanga Azumah Prosper is a recent graduate of the University of Professional Studies Accra, with a degree in BSc. Accounting.

Well beyond numbers, he is passionate about social change and youth development and believes that the assurance of a better future begins with a systematic reprogramming of the youth especially within the Northern Regions of Ghana.

This led him to co-founding the Northern Renaissance, an organization in the Tamale dedicated to actively reshaping the minds of young people through renewed self-identity and relevant skill development. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
